The Deaf and Dumb Man
DEF
noun phrase
From the Aramaic Ephphatha, “Be opened,” the word Christ spake to one deaf and having an impediment in his speech.

📖 Biblical Definition

In the coasts of Decapolis they brought unto Christ one that was deaf, and had an impediment in his speech; and they beseech Him to put His hand upon him (Mar 7:32). Christ took him aside from the multitude, and put His fingers into his ears, and He spit, and touched his tongue; and looking up to heaven, He sighed, and saith unto him, Ephphatha, that is, Be opened (Mar 7:33; Mar 7:34). And straightway his ears were opened, and the string of his tongue was loosed, and he spake plain (Mar 7:35). The dictionary marks the tender manner of this healing: Christ drew the man apart, dealt with him by signs his shut senses could perceive, and sighed as one bearing in Himself the groaning of a fallen creation, before He spake the word of power. The people were beyond measure astonished, saying, He hath done all things well: He maketh both the deaf to hear, and the dumb to speak (Mar 7:37), a saying that echoes the prophecy of the day when the ears of the deaf shall be unstopped and the tongue of the dumb sing (Isa 35:5). So the Scripture teaches the divine power and the gentle compassion of Christ together, who opens not only stopped ears but the deaf and dumb soul, that it may hear the word of God and speak His praise; for by nature men are deaf to the gospel until He say, Be opened, and the loosed tongue confess Him Lord.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A man deaf and dumb whom Christ healed with the word Ephphatha, Be opened, making him hear and speak plain.

THE DEAF AND DUMB MAN, healed by Christ in Decapolis.

He was deaf and had an impediment in his speech.

📖 Key Scripture

Mar 7:34 — "And looking up to heaven, he sighed, and saith unto him, Ephphatha, that is, Be opened."

Mar 7:35 — "And straightway his ears were opened, and the string of his tongue was loosed, and he spake plain."

Mar 7:37 — "And were beyond measure astonished, saying, He hath done all things well: he maketh both the deaf to hear, and the dumb to speak."

Isa 35:5 — "Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf shall be unstopped."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A miracle of Christ; the opening of deaf ears shews His power to unstop the soul deaf to the gospel.

expand to see more

The healing of the deaf and dumb man has drawn little redefinition from the present age, surviving as one of the tender signs recorded by Mark. The dictionary records it that the reader may mark the gentle manner of Christ, who dealt with the man by signs his shut senses could perceive, and the power of the word that opened his ears.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that Christ opens what is shut, both the stopped ear and the deaf and dumb soul. He sighed as one bearing the groaning of a fallen creation, then spake the word, Ephphatha, Be opened, and the man heard and spake plain, fulfilling the prophecy that the ears of the deaf shall be unstopped. So the dictionary draws the sign: by nature men are deaf to the gospel and dumb in praise, until Christ say, Be opened; and when He speaks, the ears are unstopped to hear the word of God and the loosed tongue confesses Him Lord. He hath done all things well.
